subject: Operational snapback playbook for on-prem VPC deployment
messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Tom Ellis <tom.ellis@nexacloud.io>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational snapback playbook for on-prem VPC deployment

Tom / Rina,

Attached is the first draft of the operational "snapback" playbook we discussed for the on‑prem VPC install. This is intended as the runbook operators will use if the primary control plane becomes unreachable or we need an expedited fail‑back to a reduced-capacity data plane in the customer colo.

Summary (quick):
- Purpose: give a safe, auditable recovery path that preserves tenant isolation while restoring inference traffic with minimal risk.
- Scope: applies to dedicated on‑prem clusters running Redwood Private (single-site initial cut) — control plane and data plane separation is enforced.
- RTO target: 15 minutes for basic serving (see section 2). RPO: best‑effort (cache clear + warmup).

Key asks from you:
1) Confirm egress constraints for the NexaCloud colo (IP allowlists / NAT restrictions).
2) Confirm how long you need audit logs retained for this process (we've proposed 90 days).
3) Can you review the topology diagram and call out any cross‑connect or transit layer constraints?

I attached: snapback_runbook_v1.pdf (full steps + verification checklist) and vpc-topology-labeled.png (annotated). Please review the runbook and call out any operational gaps by EOD Thursday. If we agree, propose a dry‑run slot next week (preferably Tue/Wed morning).

Attachments: snapback_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB), vpc-topology-labeled.png (PNG, 450KB)

Thanks —
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Manager, Customer Deployments
Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 14 Apr 2026 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational snapback playbook for on-prem VPC deployment

Thanks Stephanie — appreciate the quick turnaround. I skimmed the runbook and have a couple immediate clarifications before we schedule a dry run:

- RTO/RPO: 15 minutes RTO sounds reasonable for basic serving, but we need an explicit statement about what components are read‑only during the snapback (stateful metadata, billing events, etc.). Can the runbook call those out?
- Egress logging retention: our compliance team expects 180 days for forensic logs. Is that negotiable or do we need an addendum?
- NAT / egress path: our colo requires explicit BGP communities for certain transit providers — see note on page 2 of the topology. Will Redwood be able to accept traffic over the announce we already provisioned?

I can be on a call Tuesday 14:30–16:00 PDT or Wednesday 09:00–11:00 PDT. If Jonas wants to join the technical part, happy to do the session.

Tom — quick technical notes inline and a short ops checklist. I reviewed the runbook and topology: overall this covers the right sequence but a few gaps we should close before dry run.

1) Explicitly mark which control plane APIs will be unavailable during snapback. Suggest adding a short table:
   - /admin/tenants (read-only)
   - /admin/billing (queued, forwarding enabled)
   - /infer (serving) — routed to reduced-capacity pool

2) KV cache handling: runbook currently suggests full KV flush + cache warmup. That works but add a step to snapshot current KVs (local) before clearing — easier forensic recovery.

3) BGP / egress: we can accept the announced prefixes if NexaCloud confirms the BGP community tags. If not, fallback is NAT via transit provider B with ACL 10.23.0.0/24.

4) Verification checklist (operational):
   - Control plane followers: confirm 3/3 quorum or switched to read-only mode
   - Serving endpoints: smoke test (3 sample prompts) to validated endpoints behind the reduced pool
   - Observability: ensure token-level cost and latency traces are captured and exported to your s3 bucket (drive link in runbook)

I pasted Tom's question about logs below for reference: 
> "Egress logging retention: our compliance team expects 180 days for forensic logs. Is that negotiable or do we need an addendum?"

Answer: we can surface 180 days for exported customer logs on a case-by-case basis; will need an SOC2 evidence addendum (Kimberly to confirm). For internal event logs we keep 30 days by default.

I'll update the runbook with the above and push v1.1 to the Drive link.

Jonas Weber
Principal SRE, Deployments
jonas_weber@redwood.com

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Operational snapback playbook for on-prem VPC deployment

Tom / team — thanks for the thoughtful questions. From a Trust & Security perspective:

- Logs: we can support 180 days retention for exported egress/audit logs if NexaCloud signs the compliance addendum. I'll attach the template (DocuSign) and the specific evidence requirements.
- SOC2 evidence: please send the specific controls you require; we will mark the runbook steps that generate artifacts for SOC2 (audit trail, signature, operator id).
- Accepting BGP communities: fine so long as the transit announcement matches the allowed list in the attached topology. If we see mismatched announces we will fail closed and route through fallback NAT.

Next steps (action items):
1) Stephanie: update runbook -> v1.1 with Jonas's clarifications and add explicit controls mapping.
2) Tom / Rina: review addendum I will send via DocuSign and confirm the BGP community list.
3) I'll coordinate with Compliance to pre-approve the 180-day export for this account pending signed addendum.

I've attached a pack of recent evidence we keep for similar customers: evidence-egress-logs.tgz (contains sample syslog snippets and export manifest).

Attachments: evidence-egress-logs.tgz (TAR, 2.6MB)

Kimberly Park
Head of Trust & Security
Redwood Inference
